articles.title: Rochdale AFC Faces Accrington Stanley in League Two Clash
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC will play against Accrington Stanley in a League Two match on September 18, 2026, as both teams seek to improve their standings in the league.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC is set to face Accrington Stanley in a League Two match on September 18, 2026. The game will take place at the Wham Stadium, home of Accrington Stanley, and is expected to draw a competitive crowd as both teams aim to secure vital points in the league.

Currently, Rochdale is looking to bounce back after a series of mixed results in the league. The team has been working hard in training to improve their performance and secure a win against their rivals. Accrington Stanley, on the other hand, has also been striving for consistency and will be keen to leverage home advantage in this fixture.

Kick-off is scheduled for 3:00 PM, and fans are encouraged to arrive early to avoid congestion. Tickets are available through both clubs' official websites, and supporters are reminded to check for any last-minute updates regarding team news or potential changes to the match schedule.

This match is significant for both teams as they look to climb the League Two table. A win for Rochdale could provide a much-needed boost in confidence, while Accrington Stanley will be eager to maintain their momentum at home. Local fans are looking forward to an exciting encounter as the season progresses.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC and Oldham Athletic Issue Joint Message Ahead of League Two Fixture
articles.excerpt: Micky Mellon describes the Oldham Athletic versus Rochdale derby as a significant fixture, highlighting its competitive spirit and the passion of both sets of supporters ahead of their latest clash.
articles.content_html:
Micky Mellon, the manager of Oldham Athletic, has hailed the upcoming derby against Rochdale as a ‘cracking’ fixture, reflecting on the intense rivalry between the two neighbouring clubs. Mellon made these remarks ahead of the latest clash, which will see approximately 2,000 Oldham supporters travelling to support their team.

This match marks the fifth encounter between the two sides during Mellon’s tenure, with their first meeting occurring on October 21, 2023, which ended in a thrilling seven-goal match that Oldham won. Mellon expressed that this initial experience gave him a clear understanding of the significance of the derby to both clubs and their fans.

In his comments, Mellon admitted that he was not fully aware of the derby's importance prior to his arrival at Oldham. However, he quickly realised its significance during the lead-up to his first game as manager. He described the atmosphere as having a 'lovely bit of spice' and emphasised that he looks forward to the competitive nature of the fixture, which he believes is special.

As the teams prepare to face each other again, fans are eager to see if Oldham can extend their unbeaten league run against Rochdale, adding further excitement to this local rivalry.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC installs 26 male sanitary bins to support fans after prostate cancer treatment
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC has installed 26 specially designed male incontinence bins at the Crown Oil Arena and joined Prostate Cancer UK and phs Group's BOG STANDARD Charter through the Back in the Game campaign.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has installed 26 specially designed sanitary bins in men's toilets at the Crown Oil Arena as part of a national drive to make live sport more accessible to men living with incontinence, including some who have undergone treatment for prostate cancer.

The club launched its involvement in the Back in the Game initiative at its home opener against Crawley Town, becoming the latest sporting organisation to sign up to the BOG STANDARD Charter run by Prostate Cancer UK and hygiene services provider phs Group.

Tobi Adebayo-Rowling helped launch the initiative ahead of the match alongside Dale director Richard Knight and Jez Williams of phs Group.

The campaign focuses on a practical problem which can prevent some men from returning to football grounds and other public venues after cancer treatment: finding a suitable place to dispose of male incontinence products discreetly and hygienically.

Rochdale AFC says specially designed bins have now been installed across its male toilets. The club has received Bronze accreditation under the BOG STANDARD Charter, which represents the installation of appropriate sanitary bins for men.

Silver accreditation also requires male incontinence products to be made available, while Gold adds a commitment to promoting awareness of prostate cancer and incontinence.

Richard Knight, who has personal experience of prostate cancer, said the club wanted supporters to feel able to return to the activities and social connections that matter to them following treatment.

He said: ‘Inclusion is important to us at the Club, and we didn’t ever want to think of any of our fans being unable to join.’

Mr Knight said seeing friends, spending time with family and attending matches can all form part of getting back into everyday life after treatment, and that the club wanted to remove a practical barrier for supporters.

WHY THE BINS MATTER

Urinary incontinence can affect men for a range of reasons and can occur following some treatments for prostate cancer. Men who use absorbent pads may need access to a sanitary bin large enough to dispose of them discreetly when away from home.

Prostate Cancer UK says prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in men in the UK. Its current risk information states that around one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer during their lifetime, rising to around one in four Black men.

The charity has argued that a lack of suitable disposal facilities in men's toilets can cause anxiety and embarrassment and, in some cases, discourage people from going out or returning to activities they previously enjoyed.

Nick Ridgman, Head of Support Services at Prostate Cancer UK, said the campaign is intended to make public venues more welcoming for men living with urinary incontinence and welcomed Rochdale AFC's decision to join.

The Back in the Game campaign specifically works with sports clubs because attending live sport can be an important part of people's social lives and routines. Campaign organisers said that, as of the Rochdale launch, 177 sports clubs across the UK had signed up to the BOG STANDARD, with 873 specially designed sanitary bins for men installed through the initiative.

Matthew Brabin, chief executive of phs Group, said some men can feel anxious about leaving home after prostate cancer treatment when they are uncertain whether suitable facilities will be available. He said the campaign aims to remove that barrier and help people resume normal social activities.

The wider Dispose with Dignity campaign, run by phs Group with Prostate Cancer UK since 2023, has called for better provision for men with incontinence in public toilets.

SUPPORT FOR MEN IN ROCHDALE

Anyone worried about their prostate cancer risk, going through treatment or living with its effects can contact Prostate Cancer UK's Specialist Nurses on 0800 074 8383. The charity also provides information and support through its website.

People with new or persistent urinary symptoms should seek medical advice. Urinary problems do not necessarily mean prostate cancer, but symptoms should be assessed appropriately rather than self-diagnosed.

Rochdale AFC's decision means supporters who need to dispose of male incontinence products can now do so in designated bins within the Crown Oil Arena's male toilets.

Further information about the Back in the Game campaign is available through phs Group, while prostate cancer information and support is available from Prostate Cancer UK.

Do facilities such as these make local sports venues easier to use? Rochdale Daily welcomes readers' experiences at news@rochdaledaily.co.uk.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Netball launched as Rochdale Netball Club joins Dale family
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Netball Club is becoming Rochdale AFC Netball in a new partnership with Rochdale AFC and its Community Trust, bringing nearly 200 weekly players into the club's wider sporting family.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Netball Club is joining the Rochdale AFC family under a new identity as Rochdale AFC Netball, in a partnership designed to grow the sport and create more opportunities for women, girls and the wider community across the borough.

The agreement brings together Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and one of the borough's established community sports clubs under the wider 'Our Teams' banner.

Rochdale Netball Club currently runs teams from under-six level through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court each week. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the organisations hope to strengthen the route from school participation into junior and adult club netball while also expanding opportunities in coaching, volunteering and leadership.

The partnership is expected to support new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing and volunteer development. The shared Rochdale AFC identity could also open up additional opportunities for sponsorship, commercial support, community events and promotion through the football club.

Amy Williams, Chair of Rochdale AFC Netball, described the move as a fantastic opportunity for both the club and the sport locally, saying joining the Rochdale AFC family would provide a stronger platform to grow the game and inspire more women and girls to become involved.

Rochdale AFC chief executive Laura Thomas, herself a former netball player, said she was thrilled to welcome the club into the wider Rochdale AFC family and stressed that the club's ambition to build a thriving community extends beyond football.

Ryan Bradley, Community Director at Rochdale AFC Community Trust, said the football club, charity and netball club shared common values and could combine their respective strengths. He said bringing the organisations together under one brand would raise netball's profile in Rochdale and strengthen support for volunteers, coaches, community outreach and school work.

Rochdale AFC Netball will be based at Edgar Wood. The Community Trust also pointed to plans for the Community Football and Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee, saying the geographical proximity of the projects made closer cooperation a natural step.

The move follows a wider trend in British sport in which professional football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to increase visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the organisations say their approach will remain community focused and open to people of all ages.

Further information about Rochdale AFC Netball teams, programmes and opportunities to get involved is expected to be announced in due course.

articles.title: Councillor Daniel Meredith backs stronger Hornets partnership after Superhero Day
articles.excerpt: Balderstone and Kirkholt councillor Daniel Meredith has praised Rochdale Hornets' Superhero Day and highlighted talks about how the club and council can work together to strengthen rugby and community spirit across the borough.
articles.content_html:
Balderstone and Kirkholt councillor Daniel Meredith has praised Rochdale Hornets' Superhero Day after spending the afternoon at the club's council-sponsored fixture with his family.

Meredith attended the Hornets men's match against Whitehaven, although the afternoon produced mixed fortunes for Rochdale's teams.

The men's side narrowly lost to Whitehaven, while the Hornets women recorded a victory against Leigh Miners. Meredith joked that he may have been the day's 'jinx', having watched the men's defeat but missed the women's win while his daughter Meadhbh was having her afternoon nap.

Despite the result, Meredith described it as a great afternoon and said the council-sponsored match provided an opportunity to discuss the relationship between Rochdale Hornets and Rochdale Borough Council.

He said it was 'brilliant' to be at the game and to speak about how the Hornets and the council can continue working together to strengthen both rugby and community spirit across Rochdale.

The comments underline the wider community role played by Rochdale Hornets beyond results on the pitch, with the club's men's and women's teams, family matchdays and community activity providing opportunities to bring residents together around the sport.

Superhero Day added a family-focused theme to the fixture, encouraging supporters of different ages to take part in the matchday experience.

Meredith is a Labour and Co-operative councillor representing Balderstone and Kirkholt and serves as Rochdale Borough Council's cabinet member for regeneration and housing.

The men's result may not have gone Rochdale's way, but Meredith's message after the afternoon was focused firmly on the future: building on cooperation between the council and Hornets to support rugby and community life across the borough.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC recruiting for five roles across first team, academy and women's side ahead of League Two return
articles.excerpt: Promotion back to the Football League means growth off the pitch too: Dale are hiring a kit assistant, performance analysts, an academy lead coach and a women's first team physio.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has announced five vacancies across the club as it gears up for life back in the Football League.

The roles span the men's first team, the academy and the women's first team: a kit assistant, two performance analysts, a youth development phase lead coach and a women's first team physiotherapist or sports therapist.

The recruitment drive is a direct consequence of the club's growth. Jim McNulty's side won promotion back to Sky Bet League Two at Wembley in May, ending three seasons in the National League, and a return to the EFL brings bigger demands across every department - from matchday operations to sports science and the academy.

The kit assistant role, focused on the men's first team, is aimed at someone passionate about providing excellent service across the club's teams, with applications closing at 5pm on Friday 14 August. The club is also seeking a men's first team performance analysis work placement student for the 2026/27 season - a role suited to a student taking a sandwich year in an undergraduate degree, though masters students and recent graduates seeking industry experience will be considered.

On the academy side, Rochdale is recruiting a youth development phase lead coach. Applicants must hold a UEFA A Licence and relevant youth coaching qualifications, with previous experience in a professional academy environment an advantage. The club has said academy positions are subject to a Category 3 licence under the Elite Player Performance Plan being awarded this summer - a significant step for an academy that has long punched above its weight in producing first-team players.

The women's first team is recruiting a physiotherapist or sports therapist on a part-time, sessional basis, covering all women's first team fixtures, at least one training session a week, and injury rehabilitation and gym-based work.

The vacancies come with the 2026/27 campaign only just under way. Dale opened their season with a Carabao Cup preliminary round trip to Tranmere Rovers, and the League Two campaign is in its opening days - far too early for the table to tell us anything meaningful about how the newly promoted side will fare. The summer has brought new faces to Sandy Lane, including French midfielder Gomez-Mancini, midfielder Humbles, and Jason Taylor joining the coaching staff.

Full job adverts, including details of how to apply, are available on the club's website at rochdaleafc.co.uk, with any further academy vacancies listed on the EFL's iRecruit platform.

articles.title: New grassroots club Heywood Hurricanes FC appeals for raffle prizes to keep football free for every child
articles.excerpt: A brand-new junior football club with one simple goal - making the game accessible to every child regardless of family finances - is asking local businesses to donate raffle prizes.
articles.content_html:
A brand-new grassroots football club in Heywood is appealing to local businesses for raffle prizes as it works to keep the game affordable for every child who wants to play.

Heywood Hurricanes FC has been set up with what it calls one simple goal: to make football accessible for every child. The club says every young player deserves the opportunity to enjoy football, make friends, build confidence and be part of a team - regardless of their family's financial circumstances.

Rather than leaning on sponsorship from the outset, the club is trying to raise funds itself. "As a brand-new club, we're under no illusion that sponsorships are easy to come by," the Hurricanes said. "We know local businesses receive lots of requests, and we completely understand that not everyone is in a position to help financially."

Over the coming weeks the club will hold a raffle to help ease the financial burden on its families and keep costs as low as possible for players. It is asking whether any local businesses would be willing to donate a prize - a voucher, gift hamper, experience, service, or anything else. Every donation, big or small, the club says, will make a genuine difference.

The appeal comes at a time when many families are struggling with the cost of children's sport. Subs, kit, boots and travel add up quickly, and money is increasingly the reason children drop out of the game. By fundraising to keep its own costs down, the Hurricanes hope no child in Heywood is priced off the pitch.

"Your generosity will help us provide opportunities for children to play the game they love without additional financial pressure on their parents, especially at a time when many families are finding things incredibly tough," the club said.

Anyone who would like to support Heywood Hurricanes, or who knows someone who might be able to help, can get in touch by messaging the club's Facebook page.
articles.legal_disclaimer: This article is based on an appeal published by Heywood Hurricanes FC. Rochdale Daily has no involvement in the raffle; anyone wishing to donate should contact the club directly.

articles.title: Littleborough RUFC invites more girls to discover rugby as women's game continues to boom
articles.excerpt: Littleborough RUFC is inviting girls from Year 6 to under-18 level to try rugby this summer, as the sport continues to grow in popularity thanks to the success of England's Red Roses and increasing awareness of the physical and mental health benefits of team sport.
articles.content_html:
Littleborough Rugby Union Football Club is encouraging girls from across Rochdale borough to give rugby a try this summer, as participation in the women's and girls' game continues to grow at every level of the sport.

The club is holding open training sessions every Tuesday from 6pm until 7pm at its Rakewood Road ground in Littleborough, welcoming girls from Year 6 through to under-18 level. Organisers say there is no commitment required, with players of all abilities invited to come along, meet new friends and experience rugby in a supportive and inclusive environment.

The sessions are designed to introduce newcomers to the sport while allowing experienced players to develop their skills in a fun, welcoming atmosphere. Coaches are keen to stress that previous rugby experience is not necessary, with the emphasis firmly on enjoyment, teamwork and building confidence.

Over the past decade, girls' rugby has experienced remarkable growth across England. The Rugby Football Union has invested heavily in the women's and girls' game, with thousands more young people now playing regularly at schools and grassroots clubs. Many local clubs have expanded their junior girls' sections in response to increasing demand, creating more opportunities than ever before for young female players.

The sport has also benefited from the growing profile of the Red Roses, England's national women's rugby team. Consistently ranked among the best teams in the world, the Red Roses have inspired a new generation of players through their success on the international stage. Record-breaking attendances at Women's Six Nations matches and Rugby World Cup fixtures have demonstrated just how rapidly interest in women's rugby has grown, with elite players increasingly becoming role models for young girls considering taking up the sport.

That success at the highest level has filtered down into communities across the country. Grassroots clubs such as Littleborough RUFC have seen increasing interest from girls looking to get involved, whether for competition, fitness or simply to make new friends.

Beyond the physical benefits of exercise, rugby is widely recognised for the positive impact it can have on mental wellbeing. Taking part in team sports has been linked to reduced feelings of isolation, improved self-esteem and greater confidence, while the friendships formed through regular training and matches often provide valuable support networks for young people.

Coaches also point to the life skills rugby helps develop. Communication, resilience, leadership, discipline and respect for teammates and opponents are central values within the game, with many parents saying participation helps children grow in confidence both on and off the pitch.

The social aspect of rugby is another major attraction. Unlike many sports where players can feel under pressure from the outset, grassroots rugby clubs often place a strong emphasis on creating welcoming environments where everyone can progress at their own pace. That approach is reflected in Littleborough's message that all abilities are welcome and that there is no obligation to commit after attending a session.

The club hopes more girls from across Rochdale, Littleborough, Milnrow, Wardle and the surrounding communities will take the opportunity to experience the sport over the summer. Open training sessions allow newcomers to meet coaches and players, learn the basics and decide whether rugby is the right fit for them before the new season begins.

Training takes place every Tuesday between 6pm and 7pm at Littleborough RUFC, OL15 0AP. Girls in Year 6 through to under-18 level are invited to attend, with organisers encouraging anyone interested to simply come along and give it a go. For further information, prospective players or parents can contact Andy on 07990 744348.

As women's rugby continues to enjoy unprecedented growth across England, clubs such as Littleborough RUFC are hoping to inspire the next generation of players while demonstrating that the game offers far more than competition alone. For many young people, it can provide lasting friendships, improved wellbeing, greater confidence and the chance to become part of a thriving local sporting community.

articles.title: White Ribbon Football Tournament returns to Rochdale for 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced the return of its annual White Ribbon Football Tournament, bringing together teams from across the authority to promote the campaign to end violence against women and girls.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that its annual White Ribbon Football Tournament will return on Tuesday 4 August 2026, bringing together teams from across the council in support of the White Ribbon campaign.

Before kick-off, participating teams will take the White Ribbon pledge, reaffirming their commitment to helping end violence against women and girls.

The council is a White Ribbon accredited organisation and says the tournament has been organised entirely by members of staff in their own time to raise awareness of the campaign and encourage conversations around preventing abuse and violence.

Residents are encouraged to attend and cheer on the teams throughout the day. While places in the tournament itself are limited, spectators are welcome.

The tournament takes place at Heywood Sports Village on Tuesday 4 August 2026, and spectators are welcome.

The White Ribbon campaign works to engage men and boys in preventing violence against women and girls by promoting positive attitudes, respectful relationships and challenging harmful behaviours.

articles.title: Young bowlers invited to take part in Syke Bowling Club fun day
articles.excerpt: Syke Bowling Club is inviting young people from across Greater Manchester to a free Junior Fun Day featuring crown green bowling, prizes, refreshments and activities aimed at introducing more children to the sport.
articles.content_html:
Young people from across Greater Manchester are being invited to try crown green bowling at a free junior fun day taking place at Syke Bowling Club this weekend. The event is designed to introduce children and teenagers to the sport in a relaxed and welcoming environment, with food, drinks, prizes and coaching all included.

The Junior Fun Day will take place on Sunday, 2 August, at Syke Bowling Club on Dewhirst Road, Rochdale, with activities beginning at 11am. Organisers say the event is open to all juniors aged 18 and under, whether they have played crown green bowling before or are trying it for the first time.

Throughout the day, young participants will have the opportunity to take part in friendly bowling activities, meet other players and develop new skills under the guidance of club members. Organisers hope the event will encourage more young people to become involved in a sport that has a long history across Rochdale and the wider North West.

Prizes will be awarded during the event, including cash prizes, sweets and chocolate, while every junior attending will receive complimentary food, drinks and snacks. The organisers say the emphasis is on having fun, making new friends and giving children the confidence to have a go in an informal setting.

The event is also being used to appeal for local businesses and organisations to support junior bowling. Syke Bowling Club is seeking sponsors to help fund prizes and refreshments, saying contributions of any size would be welcomed to help expand opportunities for young players and support future events.

Grassroots sports clubs play an important role in communities by providing affordable activities, encouraging exercise and helping young people build confidence and friendships. Crown green bowling, while often associated with older generations, has seen clubs across the region working to attract younger players in an effort to secure the sport's long-term future.

Anyone interested in attending or finding out more can contact Lisa on 07900 493969. Organisers are encouraging families to come along, support the event and discover a sport that can be enjoyed by people of all ages.

With free refreshments, prizes and a welcoming atmosphere on offer, Syke Bowling Club hopes the Junior Fun Day will inspire the next generation of bowlers while showcasing one of Rochdale's long-established community sports clubs.
